jobs.title: NRO 2027 Dr. Chris Scolese Summer Internship Program at National Reconnaissance Office (NRO)
jobs.description: Employer: National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) Expires: 10/28/2026 WE ARE THE NROFor over 60 years, the NRO has developed, acquired, launched, and operated the satellites that are the foundation for America's advantage and strength in space. Using a diversified architecture of spacecraft, NRO collects and delivers the best space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance content on the planet. Learn more at nro.gov.Basic Eligibility For A Position With The NROBe a U.S. CitizenBe suitable for federal employment, as determined by a background investigationBe able to obtain and hold a TS/SCI security clearance, including a polygraphHave favorable results on a pre-employment drug testRegister for the Selective Service System if male, over 18 years of age and born after Dec 31, 1959NRO Summer Intern ProgramAre you ready to learn what it takes to be a member of our dynamic and multifaceted team of skilled professionals? Apply to participate in NRO's Dr. Chris Scolese Summer Internship Program today! We're actively seeking motivated highly qualified candidates in the Contracting, Financial Management and Technical Career Field. To learn more about these careers please click here. The NRO Summer Internship Program provides students pursuing education with paid opportunities to work at the NRO and explore career paths related to their academic field of study or career interest. Interns will receive training and guidance to prepare them to support NRO projects and initiatives.Summer interns are full-time employees on a temporary appointment for the period of 10 weeks between June and August. With a successful evaluation at the end of the summer, there may be an opportunity to return during subsequent summers based on mission requirements, continued eligibility, and the student's availability.What You Will Be DoingIntern Projects: Each intern will be given a project to complete that aligns with mission need. Specific duties will expose individuals to independent and team-oriented work opportunities. Each intern performs under direct supervision and will be provided feedback on a regular and timely basis.Professional Development and Training: Throughout the summer, NRO interns will have the opportunity to participate in a variety of professional development and training experiences. Some of these events include speaker series with NRO seniors, Security Q&A sessions, and NRO mission overviews.Who May ApplyTo be eligible for the program, the requirements include:Be enrolled full-time in an undergraduate or graduate degree program at an accredited college or university.Have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.Undergraduates must have a completed a minimum of 24 credit hours at the time of application.Provide an unofficial transcript at the time of application and an official transcript upon acceptance into the program from the academic institution.Be available for an interview and other applicable processing.NRO prohibits illegal drug involvement during employment, regardless of state level legalization, and requires a passing pre-employment drug screening. Prior drug use is carefully evaluated.Be available, and geographically located near Chantilly, Virginia for the 10-week summer program from June – August.Preferred qualifications include:Strong oral and written communication skills.Good organization and planning skills and be able to demonstrate effective project coordination and implementation based on past work or school experiences.Possess deductive reasoning skills and be able to analyze and synthesize information for problem-solving.What You Need To ApplyRequired – Resume and TranscriptIn order to qualify for this position, your resume and transcripts must provide sufficient evidence of experience and/or education relevant to the specific position for which you are being considered. Your resume will be evaluated based on the following criteria: range of occupational skills relevant to the position, alignment of education and/or work experience to the position, evidence of your experience collaborating with others, and evidence of your experience presenting information-communication skills. Please be clear and concise when describing your experience.Please upload a .pdf copy of your current transcript from the institution you are currently attending. If you have started a graduate program but have not completed your first semester, you must submit your conferred undergraduate degree, along with proof of enrollment in a full-time graduate program.Although NRO will accept unofficial transcripts at the time of the application, an official transcript is required to receive a final job offer. The official transcript will show your full-time enrollment into a program for the Fall (2026) semester of the internship year.Applicants submitting a resume that exceeds the two-page limit per OPM Memorandum, “Merit Hiring Plan,” dated May 29, 2025, https://www.opm.gov/chcoc/latest-memos/merit-hiring-plan.pdf will not be eligible for consideration. For more information regarding resume writing, see “Guidance for Applicants on 2-Page Resume” and visit the Resume Help Center.We cannot accept transcripts with limited information. When uploading your transcript, ensure it includes the following information:Your NameCollege/University NameOverall GPANumber of course creditsLocationsChantilly, Virginia (All positions)Buckley Air Force Base, Colorado (Technical Career Field only)Fort Belvoir, Virginia (Technical Career Field only)White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico (Technical Career Field only)Salary2026 Salary Range for Washington D.C. Metro Area:Working towards:Bachelor's Degree: GG-06, Step 05 - $58,884 per yearMaster's Degree: GG-07, Step 05 - $65,435 per yearDoctorate: GG-09, Step 05 - $80,041 per yearFederal pay is a combination of base and locality pay which is based on the geographic location of where you work.These positions are Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS) positions in the Expected Service under Title 10 USC 1601.Application InformationPlease review instructions prior to completing the application and answer all question carefully. Please review the description for the job you are applying for:Technical Provides technical expertise in support of acquisition, operations, mission support, launch, and other NRO missions. Offers knowledge and experience in a broad range of technical domains and specialties including research, design, development, integration and testing, program management, launch, operations, maintenance, and disposal of cutting-edge overhead intelligence systems for national security. Examples of accepted educational pursuits for jobs in this career field include:Aerospace EngineeringArtificial Intelligence/Machine LearningComputer ScienceData ScienceElectrical EngineeringGeneral EngineeringInformation TechnologyMathematicsMechanical EngineeringOperations ResearchProgram AnalysisWhat You Will Be DoingNRO Interns (GG 6-9) will receive training and guidance in the following opportunities:Prepares and evaluates plans and designs for engineering projects; researches trends and patterns; conducts technical analysis; evaluates the value and applicability of new technology; and provides engineering expertise and advice on program planning over a broad range of engineering, architecture or scientific programsSupports the management of issues and risks to balance cost, schedule and technical performanceSupports the development of new methods and criteria, procedures and/or instructions for engineering, architecture or scientific problems; proposes new policies and practicesProvides recommendations on engineering, architecture or scientific problems, programs, and functions to a broad customer baseSupports the planning, development, and implementation of crucial projects and segments of NRO programsSupports the development and modification of analytic models and methods to meet the requirements of cost, performance, and effectiveness studies and variance analysesGathers historical cost, performance and effectiveness data and establishes relationships between system characteristics and design criteriaConducts extensive systemic exploration of problems by an operations research approach; conducts analysis of alternatives, presents trend analysis data ascertaining potential problem areasSynthesizes science and technology capabilities to create new concepts and prototypes with guidanceDevelops draft test and evaluation plans with supervisory assistance; participates in the test and evaluation campaignsContracts Ensures that contractual baselines are in compliance with Federal and NRO regulations, policies, and standards. A Contract Specialist serves as a Business Advisor, who in coordination with Acquisition Program Management, assist in developing and implanting acquisition strategies and requirements documents, contract management (negotiations, administration, and etc.), and monitor contractor performance throughout the lifecycle, ensuring overall mission success. Example jobs in this career field include:Contract SpecialistWhat You Will Be DoingNRO Interns (GG 6-9) will receive training and guidance in the following opportunities:Support management on all aspects of contract management, including contract information, solicitation, negotiation, cost analysis, administration, termination and closeoutPlan, develop, and establish procurement plans strategies, and approaches for acquisition projectsSupport the developments of procurement objectives for the program regarding competition and price range; construct the contract vehiclePrepare statements of work, acquisition plans, source selection plans and solicitation documentsResponsible for contract administration functions following award throughout the contract life cycleMonitor and ensure contractor performance in accordance with the terms of the contractSupport negotiations and issue contract modification driven by technological advances or upgrade operational requirementsFinancial Management Supports the NRO in formulation and execution of the NRO budget. Works with program management to ensure program closure. These responsibilities include analyzing program and/or acquisition data through qualitative and quantitative techniques, identifying and evaluating options to solve program budget issues, certifying funding availability, providing regulatory and procedural guidance, and providing overall financial management support to the NRO's directorates and offices. Examples of job responsibilities in this career field include:Budget Formulation – forecasting budget needs for future years by planning/balancing limited resourcesBudget Execution – day-to-day budget actions/reporting and contractor performance analysisFiscal Law & Policy – Execute budgets within legal parameters and policy; unique to federal governmentFinancial Systems – learn/leverage available systems/databases to perform analysis supporting decisions related to budgetWhat You Will Be DoingNRO Interns (GG 6-9) will receive training and guidance in the following opportunities:Financial Concepts of NROFund commitment, obligation and expenditureOrganization specific financial requirement tools and resource planningTransactions and financial tools to execute program resourcesAppropriations Law to include purpose, time, and amount as they relate to budgetsOrganizational budget hierarchy and alignment for resource management and accounting (financial statement) purposesExecution metrics and oversight reporting of obligations and expenditures.Acquisitions Support to NRO ProgramsContract types and financial requirement planningContract deliverables and financial analysis/forecastingSpend plans and forecasting of funding needsTrial PeriodAll new DCIPS employees will be required to serve a two-year trial period.Veteran's PreferenceDoW Components with DCIPS positions apply Veteran's Preference to preference eligible candidates as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 USC, in accordance with the procedures provided in DoW (DoD) Instruction 1400.25, Vol 2005, DCIPS Employment and Placement. If you are a veteran claiming Veteran's Preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 USC, you must submit documents verifying your eligibility upon request.Equal Employment Opportunity PolicyThe United States Government does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, political affiliation, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, genetic information, age, membership in an employee organization, retaliation, parental status, military service, or other non-merit factor.Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) for federal employees & job applicantsReasonable Accommodation PolicyFederal agencies must provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with disabilities where appropriate. jobs.title: Accounting Intern (Spring 2027) at Ryan & Wetmore, P.C.
jobs.description: Employer: Ryan & Wetmore, P.C. Expires: 10/28/2026 ABOUT THE ROLE Ryan & Wetmore, PC is seeking Accounting Interns for Spring 2027 (January-April) for our offices in Bethesda MD, Vienna VA, and Frederick MD. Interns are part-time employees and are expected to work roughly 20 hours per week. In this role, you will work across multiple industries on engagements in tax, attest, and accounting, with clients from entrepreneurs to growing businesses. This position offers hands-on experience and the opportunity to develop expertise in areas such as tax strategy, audit & assurance, and client accounting services. The intern experience at Ryan & Wetmore is built upon each intern’s areas of interest in accounting, consulting, and tax. We work with interns to develop both professional goals for the internship, striving to provide a meaningful and practical experience. Interns begin their time with Ryan & Wetmore by receiving basic training on the IT systems and software used for accounting and assurance engagements, tax return preparation, researching, and timekeeping. After gaining an understanding of how the office functions, interns begin working on accounting and other tasks. Internships include some administrative duties, such as scanning and saving pertinent client-related information. WHO YOU ARE Are you ready to jumpstart your career in the world of accounting, tax law, and economics? Ryan & Wetmore, PC, a leading accounting firm in the greater Washington DC region that specializes in tax planning and business growth strategies, is seeking enthusiastic and driven individuals to join our team. If you're a motivated self-starter with a passion for accounting, a thirst for knowledge in tax regulations, and an interest in the intersection of politics and economics, this opportunity is for you. WHO WE ARE For over 30 years, Ryan & Wetmore has provided accounting, tax, and consulting services through our team of innovative thought leaders who are committed to our approach, providing excellent services to clients of a diverse range of industries all over the US. We are a member of the BDO Alliance, which allows us to combine the expertise of a large, industry-leading organization with the personalized touch of a small, client-centric environment. POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES Perform audit procedures, over cash, A/R, inventories property and equipment, prepaid, A/P, accrued expenses, debt and general income statement accounts in client financial statements and propose adjusting journal entries when needed Review accounting transactions and consider appropriate application of generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) Prepare financial statement footnotes (on areas audited) and internal control observations and recommendations Research fundamental issues using online tools Meet client service expectations by adhering to time budgets, maintaining positive communications, and delivering highest level of customer service to clients, including those at the executive level Perform other duties as needed on engagements and as assigned by supervisory personnel Gain an understanding of firm policies, procedures, and professional standards through observation and inquiry, and adhere to them Demonstrate a positive attitude towards the firm and profession, and represent the firm in a favorable and professional manner POSITION REQUIREMENTS Pursuing an Undergraduate or Graduate Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Economics, or related field with an anticipated graduation date no later than May 2028 Minimum 3.0 GPA Have completed minimum 90 credit hours towards B.A. / B.S. degree or equivalent from accredited university Have a desire to obtain a CPA license Proficiency with personal computers and Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to liaise internally with firm leadership, and externally with clients Excellent organizational, time management, and adaptability skills to manage multiple projects at a time, completing tasks on time to meet internal and external deadlines Basic research skills and understanding of accounting related terms and practices (e.g. the concept of billable hours, client confidentiality, professional ethics, AICPA & state societies) Integrity, dependability, and trustworthiness Sharp analytical skills and a commitment to professional development Preferred: related work or internship experience in accounting and/or client-facing roles Desire to work closely with Partners and clients to provide exceptional service Ability to maintain confidentiality of firm and client information Experience working with a team to meet deliverables and ability to thrive and adapt in a fast-paced, dynamic environment Ability to work remotely and at 1 of the 3 office locations: Bethesda MD, Frederick MD, or Vienna VA

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Content Marketing Intern (20-40hrs/week) at EF Education First
jobs.description: Employer: EF Education First Expires: 10/28/2026 About the role At EF Ultimate Break, we inspire 18–35-year-olds to join life-changing travel experiences around the world. Our travelers include college students escaping campus to bop around Europe, young professionals who’ve stockpiled PTO taking their dream trip to Japan, and everyone in between. We’re looking for a college student or recent grad with a sharp eye for digital-first creative, cultural moments, and emerging trends. Someone who can translate ideas into work that earns the attention of the next generation of travelers. From TikTok ads and CMS updates to trip launches and organizing swag for teams. you’ll have the opportunity to work on a wide range of projects that directly influence how travelers discover and experience our brand.Consider this a professional outlet for your travel obsession.This is a cross-functional role built for someone who’s organized, curious, people-oriented, and genuinely excited about how content works across channels, across teams, and across formats. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys variety and is excited to jump between hands-on tasks—from making site updates and creating graphics to QAing content and supporting day-to-day marketing projects.You’ll partner with our Growth and Creative teams to bring content to life: building landing pages, making updates in our CMS, creating and optimizing digital ads, and ensuring our brand shows up as its best across channels. You don’t need to be an expert in all of it on day one, but you do need the drive to learn fast and the people skills to work across teams. What you’ll do -Source, organize, and create content in our CMS for the Ultimate Break website, ranging from promotional graphics to content-rich landing pages and itinerary pages -Create compelling content for paid media advertising and work with the team to optimize and refine ads for stronger performance -Support content calendars, asset libraries, and documentation for your projects so nothing falls through the cracks -Leverage agentic tools to automate repetitive production tasks: generating copy variations for landing pages, adapting email content for different segments, etc.What we’re looking for Required -Some experience in content creation and comfort with learning new systems -A keen eye for design and copy to ensure consistency of our branded content across channels -A natural communicator who’s comfortable working with different teams -A hands-on comfort with AI tools; you’ve used AI agents to get work done faster, without losing sight of taste, originality, and craft. -Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail -Strong verbal and visual communication skills with the ability to interpret direction -An interest in keeping up with (and sharing!) evolving Gen Z and Millennial trendsAdditional helpful (but not mandatory) skills: Experience working with a CMS and ad platforms -Experience working with an ecommerce/DTC brand -Some knowledge of Figma and Canva -Light video, animation, or motion skillsWhy this role You’ll get visibility across nearly every marketing function: ecommerce, paid media, CRM, and branded content. We’re a team that moves fast, values good ideas and is actively investing in how AI agents can power our workflows. The practical stuff—and why it’s part of the fun• $25 per hour: This is a paid, hourly internship.• 20–40 hours per week: We’re open to interns who can contribute anywhere from 20 to 40 hours each week. Whether you’re a student with 20 hours available or a recent graduate looking for full-time hours, we’ll work together to find a schedule that fits.• On-site collaboration: During your working hours, you’ll work from the office alongside our creative and marketing teams. We believe the best ideas often come from being in the room together—sharing feedback, brainstorming, and learning from one another. About UsSome companies are in the business of banking. Others are in the business of shoes. Or sports. Or soft drinks. At EF, we're in a different kind of business. One that's a little less tangible, and a lot more important. Because our business, what we make, makes everything else possible. We're in the business of understanding. Between people. Between cultures.For over half a century we’ve been the leader in international educational programs and experiences designed to foster such understanding. Through language, cultural exchange, academic studies, and educational travel, we create the kinds of immersive experiences that challenge biases, open minds, and pave the way for a more understanding world. You’ll find our offices and schools located in some of the world’s greatest cities, and filled with smart, driven people (over 50,000 of us) who push each other to be better every day. But it’s what we do together - building greater understanding, breaking down barriers, and creating a better world - that makes all the difference. Founded in 1965 in Sweden, EF (Education First) is a global association of education companies that share a common mission of opening the world through education. EF has been recognized on Forbes 2025 and 2024 World’s Best Employers and 2024 Top Companies for Women lists, Fast Company’s 2025 Next Big Things In Tech, and was a 2024 App Store Award winner in Cultural Impact. About the TeamAt EF Ultimate Break, we’re about way more than collecting passport stamps. Our guided tours empower young adults aged 18–35 to explore a world outside their comfort zones. Each immersive tour creates experiences that last a lifetime, building bonds with fellow travelers that go beyond borders and cultures, and help bring the world a little bit closer. WARNING: Working at Ultimate Break may inspire your own desire to experience the world, good news is- we’ll help with that! Learn more about EF Ultimate Break: https://www.efultimatebreak.com/

jobs.description: Employer: RAM Aerospace Expires: 10/28/2026 RAM Aerospace is a leader in aerospace innovation, powering flight and space exploration with precision solenoids, valves, actuators, and position sensing solutions. Since 1975, we've supported missions like the Space Shuttle and continue to deliver mission-critical components for commercial, defense, and satellite systems. Headquartered in St. George, Utah, our advanced manufacturing facility produces the precision solenoids, valves, and actuators that aerospace programs worldwide depend on. Our Valencia facility extends that capability with specialized manufacturing of LVDTs and RVDTs, critical position sensing devices used across a broad range of aerospace and defense applications. As one of Southern Utah's largest employers, we drive economic growth and offer high-skilled careers in engineering and manufacturing. From both facilities, we build the future of aerospace—on time, with excellence, and as a team. Join us to work on groundbreaking technology and help shape the future of flight and space exploration. Your career takes off here!RAM Aerospace's LVDT/RVDT Intern program is built for engineering students who want more than a summer project. This is a year-round, part-time position designed to fit alongside your academic schedule, giving you sustained, meaningful exposure to the design, analysis, test, and manufacturing of Linear Variable Differential Transformers, the precision position sensing devices that aerospace and defense systems worldwide depend on. You will work directly alongside experienced engineers and technicians, contributing to real work on real hardware across multiple disciplines. By the time you finish school, you will have built a level of hands-on aerospace engineering experience that very few of your peers can match. If you are an engineering student who is eager to learn, ready to contribute, and looking for a role that grows with you through your academic career, this opportunity was built for you.Duties and ResponsibilitiesDesign & Engineering Support: Assist RAM engineers in the design and development of LVDT/RVDT components and assemblies. Support CAD modeling, drawing updates, and design documentation using 3D CAD tools, and contribute to design reviews and engineering analysis tasks as your skills and familiarity with the product grow over time.Analysis & Performance Modeling: Support engineering analysis efforts related to LVDT/RVDT performance, including electromagnetic behavior, dimensional tolerance reviews, and basic mechanical assessments. Learn to apply analytical tools and methods under the guidance of senior engineers, building a working understanding of how design decisions translate into measurable performance outcomes.Test Support & Data Collection: Assist in the setup, execution, and documentation of LVDT/RVDT performance and functional testing. Operate test equipment under supervision, collect and log test data accurately, and support the analysis and reporting of test results in a format that informs engineering decisions.Manufacturing & Assembly Support: Work alongside technicians in the assembly of LVDT/RVDT components and subassemblies, learning proper assembly techniques, workmanship standards, and the attention to detail that precision aerospace hardware demands. Support manufacturing operations in a manner that reinforces RAM's quality and FOD prevention standards at all times.Documentation & Continuous Learning: Maintain accurate records of engineering and assembly activities in accordance with RAM's quality management system requirements. Engage actively with the engineers and technicians around you, ask good questions, take ownership of your development, and bring growing capability and initiative to your work with each passing semester.RequirementsLegal: Must be able to pass a comprehensive criminal background check and drug screening.ITAR: Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum (due to ITAR requirements).Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's degree program in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a closely related field required.Minimum sophomore standing required. Junior or senior standing preferred.Basic understanding of electromagnetic or electromechanical principles gained through coursework is a plus.Exposure to 3D CAD software through coursework or personal projects preferred. SolidWorks experience a plus.Ability to read and interpret basic engineering drawings and written assembly procedures.Strong attention to detail and genuine commitment to accuracy in both hands-on work and documentation.Ability to commit to a consistent part-time schedule throughout the academic year, with flexibility to increase hours during breaks if desired.Eager to learn, self-motivated, and comfortable working in an active manufacturing and engineering environment alongside experienced professionals.Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document work accurately and collaborate effectively with engineers and technicians.We are committed to creating an environment where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally.EEO (Equal Employment Opportunity)RAM Aerospace is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.description: Employer: Iowa PBS Expires: 10/29/2026 Job DescriptionThis is a non-merit internship position. Production InternAre you ready to embark on an exciting journey with Iowa PBS, where your passion for creativity meets the power of media?Iowa PBS, Iowa's only statewide television broadcasting network, is searching for two Spring 2027 interns to join our dynamic programming and production division. If you're a college student with a passion for creativity and a desire to make a real impact on the world, our internship offers an experience that will help you achieve just that. About Us: At Iowa PBS, we're not just a network; we're on a mission to educate, inform, enrich, and inspire viewers across the state. We're the folks who bring you those unforgettable local programs, broadcast services, and innovative educational initiatives that shape the future of our communities. Our strength lies in our diverse, talented, and dedicated team members who are at the heart of our mission. When you join us, you're not just an intern; you're a future leader in the making. Role Overview: Iowa PBS is seeking two exceptional Spring 2027 interns within our production division. As a production intern, you'll dive into the world of studio cameras, teleprompters and lighting, gaining hands-on experience in operating professional-grade equipment. You'll work alongside our seasoned videographers, editors, and scenic professionals, developing expertise in the art of content creation, editing, and distribution. The goal of this internship is to empower you to:Master Video Production Techniques: Learn the ins and outs of studio and on-location video production, from camera operation to lighting setups, ensuring you have a solid foundation in the technical aspects of video creation.Editing and Post-Production Skills: Hone your editing skills using industry-standard software, transforming raw footage into polished, engaging content that captivates our audiences.Creative Storytelling: Develop your ability to craft compelling narratives, translating ideas into captivating visual stories that educate and inspire.Team Collaboration: Work closely with a diverse team of professionals, refining your collaboration, communication, and project management skills in a real-world broadcast environment.Problem Solving: Encounter and overcome challenges unique to the world of media production, cultivating a problem-solving mindset that will serve you well in any future endeavor.Audience Engagement: Gain insights into audience preferences and engagement strategies, helping you understand how to connect with viewers on a deeper level.In addition, you can expect to assist with weekly shows like Iowa Press and Market to Market, and get ready for some special projects like covering the girls and boys high school basketball championships, girls and boys high school wrestling championships, college wrestling meets across the state, Iowa's Condition of the State speech, and Iowa PBS's annual Festival pledge drive. By the end of this internship, you'll emerge with a well-rounded skill set, ready to excel in the world of media production and make a meaningful impact in your future career. Why Iowa PBS: Choosing Iowa PBS for your internship isn't just about gaining experience; it's about making a difference. It's about becoming a part of something bigger than yourself. Here, you won't just find a place to work; you'll find a community that values you for your unique ideas and perspectives you bring to the team. We're not just offering an internship; we're offering an enriching experience where every day is an opportunity to grow and shine.Ready to start your adventure with Iowa PBS? Join us as we educate, inform, enrich, and inspire Iowans. If you're passionate about driving positive change and have the dedication to excel in this role, we invite you to become part of our team. Don't miss out on this chance to be a catalyst for positive change and contribute to our vibrant community. Apply now and kickstart your rewarding internship at Iowa PBS today! Iowa PBS is an inclusive workplace and we welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences.Iowa PBS is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. jobs.description: Employer: Agate Publishing, Inc. Expires: 10/29/2026 Agate is seeking interns for its six-month on-site internship program. The internship terms are typically between January 1–June 30 (we are accepting applications now for 2027 candidates) and July 1–December 31 (we have filled these spots for 2026 and are now seeking candidates only for early 2027). Interns are asked to spend approximately 20-30 hours per week on site, depending on their availability, and receive extensive training as well as credit from their academic institution and a stipend of approximately $80 per week. We offer interns considerable flexibility in scheduling their hours during the work week, to allow them to attend school and/or hold paying jobs while also doing the internship. Agate accepts applications for internships year-round.Agate has an excellent record in helping interns find publishing industry jobs, whether in the Chicago area or elsewhere. Several Agate interns have been offered staff positions and contractor roles at the company, though there is no formal, structured intern hiring program here, and no interns are guaranteed jobs after completing the program. Most of the Agate staff who oversee our internship program have themselves been Agate interns. All Agate interns are trained in a variety of fundamental publishing and small business tasks, with an eye toward preparing them for different entry-level job opportunities in publishing. All Agate interns participate in eight intensive, in-depth training seminars during the course of the internship, for which they earn a Publishing Basics certification from our Agate Publishing Academy division. These seminars are designed to give interns a 360-degree understanding of basic trade and educational publishing functions by the time they complete the program.Qualifications: Agate only considers candidates who have completed at least half their junior year of undergraduate studies. Preference is given to enrolled students, whether undergraduate or graduate, who are able to earn credit for their Agate training internship. Strong reading, writing, and personal communication skills are essential, as is a solid grasp of English grammar and style. Previous experience in manuscript editing and/or familiarity with The Chicago Manual of Style is very welcome. Solid organizational skills and computer skills are also desired. Experience with the Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, InDesign) is a bonus but not required.The internship may entail some or all of the following responsibilities:Produce catalog and press materials, including press kits and pitches Draft and send out mass mailings Assist with publicity campaigns by communicating via email with media organizationsAssist in pre-publication market research Compile and organize media contact information Produce social media postings Help maintain office inventory Write, edit, and post website informationRead and review manuscript submissions Copyedit, proofread, and review educational and marketing contentWrite and research assessment and manuscript content Perform administrative and organizational tasksTo apply: Email a resume, cover letter, and two nonfiction writing samples, amounting to no more than 3000 words total, and—if you wish to demonstrate design experience—two design samples in PDF format, no larger than 2MB, to onsite@agatepublishing.com, with the words “On-Site Internship Application” in the subject line of the message.

jobs.title: Spring 2027 Operations and Sustainability (Paid) Intern at Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
jobs.description: Employer: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum Expires: 10/29/2026 Please note: Applications for this position will be accepted through Monday, November 2.Internship: Operations and Sustainability (Paid)For application deadlines and internship dates, please visit: Countrymusichalloffame.org/support/get-involved/internships. Museum Overview: Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum has been called the “Smithsonian of country music,” celebrated for its broad cultural impact, educational mission, and unrivaled collection of historically important artifacts. Chartered by the state of Tennessee in 1964, the Museum is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, educational organization that documents and interprets the history of country music. The Museum collects objects and archival materials that illustrate the evolving history and traditions of country music and provides diverse learning opportunities through educational programs, publications, and exhibitions. First opened in 1967 on Nashville’s Music Row, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum launched its current downtown location in 2001. In 2014, the Museum unveiled a $100 million expansion that doubled its footprint. The Museum now encompasses 350,000 square feet of exhibition galleries, archival storage, retail stores, and event space. The Museum owns Hatch Show Print, a letterpress print shop opened in 1879, and it operates Historic RCA Studio B, where Dolly Parton, Elvis Presley, and many others recorded. In addition, the Museum offers the Taylor Swift Education Center for students, teachers, and families, and dedicated performance spaces in the CMA Theater and Ford Theater, both of which regularly host nationally recognized live music and cultural events.In 2024, the Museum was awarded the prestigious National Medal of Arts by President Joe Biden. The medal is the highest award given to artists and arts institutions by the United States government. The White House Citation, which accompanied the medal, recognized the Museum’s work, which “preserves history, honors giants of the genre, and inspires future generations to write their own songs about the American story.”Internship Program Overview: The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum offers paid internships to full-time college students (undergraduate and graduate) that advance the educational goals of the intern and help to promote the Museum’s mission. The Museum’s internship program offers work-based learning opportunities that introduce college students to museum-related careers and other professions found in large cultural organizations. Internships are designed for a maximum commitment of 25 hours per week for 12 weeks with consideration given to individual university requirements. Additional adjustments to the 12-week, 25-hour schedule will be at the discretion of the internship supervisor. Educational programs which operate on a quarterly basis may be accommodated. Motivated students who are seeking hands-on experiences in a team-oriented environment will find excellent opportunities at the Museum.The application process for prospective interns includes the submission of:An online application for the specific internship you are applying for via our internal hiring systemA resumeA one-page cover letter; it is recommended that your cover letter explain how your education and experience will contribute positively to this internship and how this internship relates to your academic pursuits and/or career goals What We Offer Interns: The hourly rate for this position is $15/hr. for students pursuing a bachelor's degree; $18/hr. for students pursuing a master's degree or higher Free 24/7 downtown parking or WeGo bus pass Complimentary admission to the Museum for yourself Two complimentary Museum admission passes for friends and family useFree guided tour of Hatch Show Print, Historic RCA Studio B, and the Museum’s galleriesDiscounts at Museum stores and restaurantsFree or discounted entry to local venues including: National Museum of African American Music, the Opry, Ryman Auditorium, and more!Fun, friendly, and supportive learning environment Field Forward Stipend: Field Forward is a living and relocation stipend, offered to select candidates in addition to the paid internship, that supports students who identify as traditionally underrepresented in cultural arts careers and students with demonstrated financial need. Field Forward’s goals are to encourage diverse student engagement with the Museum and the broader museum field and to promote educational and professional experience and training to students historically underrepresented in museum and other cultural arts professions. Students must submit an additional application and demonstrate financial need (if applicable) to be considered. To learn more, including important deadlines, please visit: Countrymusichalloffame.org/support/get-involved/internships.Departmental Overview: The Operations and Sustainability department is responsible for security, housekeeping, courier services, parking, dock management, and sustainability. Our goal is to support the building in its mission of preservation, to provide flawless service to our staff and others & serve as a brand ambassador to external clients. jobs.description: Employer: Nucor Raw Materials - Raw Materials Expires: 10/30/2026 Operations Management Internship (Summer 2027)Job DetailsDivision: Nucor CorporationLocation: Louisville, Houston, Kansas City, Cincinnati, Salt Lake CityOther Available Locations: Texas; Kansas; Ohio; UtahCompensation: $27.00/hr + relocation assistance if applicable About NucorWelcome to Nucor, where our unique culture sets us apart. Joining Nucor means becoming part of North America's largest steel and steel products manufacturer, offering unmatched career opportunities and stability. We are known for our innovative sustainability practices and are the continent's largest recycler. Our vibrant culture, built on personal connections and teamwork, empowers every teammate with the freedom to innovate and contribute to our collective success. Experience a workplace where safety, efficiency, and meaningful personal connections define every day, enriching both our teammates and the communities we serve.WATCH THIS VIDEO and WATCH THIS OTHER VIDEO to get a sense of what we do, who we are, our opportunities and our work environment. What You'll Do:Safety is the most important part of all jobs within Nucor; therefore, candidates must be able to demonstrate the ability to initiate, lead, and uphold safety policies, practices, procedures, and housekeeping standards at all times. The goal of the program is to learn key facets of the operation from the ground up and understand what a career in scrap metal recycling and operations leadership could look like after graduation. Duties of the role include, but are not limited to:Participate in daily safety meetings and learn and model Nucor’s “Safety First” culture, including OSHA practices, safety programs, housekeeping, and daily operational standards.Learn scrap metal identification, buying and inspecting scrap, processing, quality control, and inventory practices.Gain exposure to day-to-day operations, transportation and logistics, and maintenance of equipment.Support daily facility operations, including material receiving and inbound and outbound coordination.Interact with teammates, managers, customers, vendors/suppliers, and other business partners to help resolve problems and support the steady delivery of products purchased or sold.Collaborate with operations leaders to understand how work is planned and directed across the organization.Review operational data, identify trends, and recommend proactive improvements to safety, productivity, cost, customer service, or other business situations.Learn how operational decisions and actions help protect company assets and profitability.Complete a summer-long business project and present recommendations to division leadership.Build effective working relationships across departments and participate in team meetings and strategic-planning activities.Expect to travel as necessary between facilities.You will work outside in extreme weather conditions in an industrial environment.Be willing to relocate post-graduation.What We're Looking For:Required:Rising junior or senior working toward a bachelor's degree, preferably in Business, Supply Chain, Operations Management, Construction Management, Management, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.Strong organizational skills with the ability to adapt to changing assignments in a fast-paced environment.Excellent verbal and written communication skills.Ability to build relationships, collaborate, and work efficiently with team members.Ability to creatively solve problems. Preferred:Continuous improvement mindset.Safety mindset.Previous internship experience.Previous leadership experience.Pay, Benefits & Career Growth- Competitive hourly pay.- Relocation assistance if applicable.- Exposure to career opportunities in scrap metal recycling after graduation.- Nucor supports teammates with benefits including Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability Insurance, 401(k) and Roth accounts, profit sharing, pay-for-performance bonuses, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement, stock program, scholarships, and more.Our Commitment to a Drug Free Workplace:Employment is contingent upon successfully passing a pre-employment drug screening, which includes both urine and hair follicle testing. jobs.description: Employer: H&R Block Expires: 10/30/2026 At H&R Block, our purpose is simple: to provide help and inspire confidence in our clients and communities everywhere. For more than 70 years, we’ve led the tax industry and we continue to evolve through our Block Next strategy, blending human expertise with digital innovation. That same commitment to care extends to our associates. When you join us, you become part of a High Performing, Connected Culture built on strong relationships, continuous learning, and a shared commitment to making a meaningful impact. We invest in your well-being through competitive pay, comprehensive benefits, and support for life both in and outside of work. Turn your classroom learning into real-world impact with H&R Block’s Embark 2027 Summer Internship Program, open to students interested in Recruiting, Recruitment Marketing, Project Management, or Talent Acquisition. jobs.title: Financial Services Data Analytics Intern at H&R Block
jobs.description: Employer: H&R Block Expires: 10/30/2026 At H&R Block, our purpose is simple: to provide help and inspire confidence in our clients and communities everywhere. For more than 70 years, we’ve led the tax industry and we continue to evolve through our Block Next strategy, blending human expertise with digital innovation. That same commitment to care extends to our associates. When you join us, you become part of a High Performing, Connected Culture built on strong relationships, continuous learning, and a shared commitment to making a meaningful impact. We invest in your well-being through competitive pay, comprehensive benefits, and support for life both in and outside of work. Turn your classroom learning into real-world impact with H&R Block’s Embark 2027 Summer Internship Program, open to students studying Finance, Economics, and Data Analytics. This 11-week paid internship offers meaningful, real-world experience that aligns with your field of study while making a valuable impact on our organization.The Embark 2027 Summer Internship runs from May 17, 2027 – July 30, 2027.You’ll work at our corporate headquarters in the heart of downtown Kansas City’s Power & Light District, where you’re just steps, or a streetcar ride, away from incredible restaurants, entertainment, and city energy. Inside our building, you’ll have access to amenities that make work-life balance easy, including an onsite Starbucks, a company dining hall with plenty of options, a free fitness center, and free parking!Program Highlights:$25/hour compensationPaid PTO during H&R Block’s annual Reboot Week (June 28 – July 2)Housing stipend provided for students whose permanent address is more than 50 miles from the KC metro The Financial Services Data Analytics & Strategy Intern will contribute to key strategic initiatives within H&R Block’s Financial Services line of business. This role offers exposure to product strategy, financial services innovation, and decision-making at the leadership level. The intern will be embedded within the Financial Services product team and will collaborate closely with product managers supporting Spruce, H&R Block’s emerging financial health platform (sprucemoney.com). Throughout the 11-week internship, under the guidance of a leader, some of the internship responsibilities will include:Conduct research and analysis to support strategic and product decisions within the Financial Services business.Analyze customer, market, competitive, and financial data to identify trends, opportunities, and areas for further exploration.Help develop financial and analytical models that measure customer value, acquisition efficiency, engagement, and other key business metrics.Evaluate existing metrics and data, identify gaps, and help develop clear, decision-useful insights and recommendations.Partner with Product, Finance, Analytics, and other cross-functional teams to explore strategic opportunities and support key Financial Services initiatives.Synthesize research, data, and business discussions into clear presentations, models, and recommendations for leadership.Gain exposure to real-world business decisions and trade-offs while receiving mentorship and taking increasing ownership of assigned work. Throughout the 11-week internship, as a part of the Embark program, interns will also participate in workshops and events that align with the program's four pillars:Professional Development: includes the basics for a professional role, everything from using Microsoft Office to setting up a Teams meeting and giving a presentation.Giveback: involves participating in Make Every Block Better community service events. The goal is to teach the importance of community, make an impact, and provide bonding time for teams.Networking: entails meeting various executives with offices at H&R Block’s headquarters, having lunch with directors and vice presidents, spending time with a mentor and getting to know people beyond their assigned department.Connected Culture: is meant to be fun and teach the importance of working hard and playing hard. H&R Block might take the interns to a Kansas City Royals game or facilitate other competitions meant to be fun or instill teamwork.

From being a socially responsible business, to investing in our Associates, we're always looking at how we can make tomorrow brighter. As an Associate, you are empowered with the freedom and tools to be yourself, to forge your own path, to build relationships across our global community, to discover the right opportunities for you to grow – all with ample support. Here, you have our ongoing commitment to your growth and development as you work across our world-famous brands. Start your journey at Mars today! Mars Snacking Research and Development Internship Experience As a Mars Snacking Research and Development Intern, you will gain exposure to the following areas: Compliance functions including scientific and regulatory affairs Product, process, or packaging development Science & Technology Sensory Work with a Functional Lead who will serve as your day-to-day, on-site mentor to provide guidance throughout the experience. What we’re looking for: An individual that is curious, passionate, and has a results-driven mindset with a hunger to learn and an ability to rapidly build strong cross-functional relationships that support our strategic R&D priorities. Enthusiastic about our iconic brands, research, innovation, and the consumer products industry Pursuing degrees in Food Science, Environmental Science, Biological Systems, Packaging or Chemical Engineering. Interested in concentrations / minors in data analytics, consumer insights, sensory. Passionate about applying robust scientific and critical thinking to solve complex problems, generate insights, and inform data-driven decisions. Eligible candidates will intern the summer prior to their final graduation date (typically rising seniors – May 2028 Graduation) or the summer prior to their junior year (rising juniors – May 2029 Graduation). Open to students legally authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future work status authorization or visa sponsorship for employment. Some of our successful interns may receive full-time offers to start their career with Mars! Some of the internship positions available might be located at a facility that processes nuts or allows dogs and cats on site. Exciting professional and social engagement activities throughout the experience that provide opportunities to network with your intern peers all the way up to senior leaders. Best-in-class training and development from Day 1, including a formal mentor, access to our in-house Mars University, and more. jobs.description: Employer: Western National Insurance Group Expires: 10/30/2026 Who are we?Western National Insurance Group is a private mutual insurance company with over 120 years of experience serving customers' property-and-casualty insurance needs in the Midwestern, Northwestern, and Southwestern United States. Known as “The Relationship Company®,” we define success as a measure of the relationships we have built over time. This program not only offers practical, hands-on opportunities and project work in partnership with our Data & Integrations team; but interns will also have the opportunity to enhance their existing skill sets through a range of professional development activities, cultivate relationships with employees and fellow interns, and participate in impactful volunteer initiatives within the community. Position Summary:As a Data Engineering Intern in our Internship Program, you will join our Data & Integrations team and gain hands-on experience supporting the systems and processes that turn business data into useful information. You will work alongside experienced data engineers and business partners while learning about enterprise data warehousing, data integration, software development, and Agile delivery practices. Potential responsibilities include:Work with technologies used in our data environment, including SQL Server, SSIS, Snowflake, Python, and other tools that support enterprise data warehousing and automation. Our team is also transitioning selected data workloads from SSIS and SQL Server toward Snowflake, providing exposure to both established and modern data engineering practices.Develop and test enhancements to data applications, ETL/ELT workflows, and supporting processes based on business requirements.Troubleshoot and debug data integration and Enterprise Data Warehousing (EDW) issues by analyzing data, reviewing code, and working with team members to identify solutions.Write clear, maintainable code and contribute to code reviews, unit testing, and other quality practices.Participate in Agile activities such as backlog refinement, work estimation, planning, and team discussions.Help identify opportunities to improve data processes, documentation, automation, and team efficiency.Create and maintain technical documentation to support learning, onboarding, ongoing maintenance, and production releases.Follow data security, privacy, quality, and change-management practices appropriate for an insurance environment.Complete special projects and other duties as assigned. What You’ll Need to Succeed:Currently pursuing a degree, certificate, or coursework in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Information Systems, Mathematics, or a related field.A passion for technology and an interest in working with, analyzing, and improving data.Basic experience with SQL and relational databases through coursework, projects, employment, or personal learning.Exposure to Python or another scripting/programming language.Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with an interest in understanding how systems and processes work.Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and nontechnical audiences.Willingness to ask questions, learn from feedback, and collaborate effectively with others.Ability to pay close attention to detail when working with data, code, and documentation.Familiarity with Agile software development practices, source control tools such as Git or GitLab, or ETL/ELT technologies such as SSIS or Snowflake is preferred but not required.Exposure to DevOps concepts, CI/CD processes, testing practices, or tools such as Docker or Jenkins is a plus.Two years of college or equivalent relevant experience is preferred. Compensation Overview:The base pay offered for this position will be $20.00/hour.More About Western National Insurance Group:Western National has long been known as “The Relationship Company®” and caring for our employees is part of that relationship commitment. We value connectiveness, empowerment, and accountability, and we believe that our employees are our biggest asset.Currently ranked as the 41st largest private company by revenue in Minnesota (Minneapolis/St. Paul Business Journal), Western National has earned accolades year-over-year as an employer of choice and garnered multiple awards for wellness in the workplace. Western National has also been named a Top Workplace by the Star Tribune for consecutive years. In addition, the Group is consistently recognized as a Ward’s 50 property-and-casualty insurance company for its outstanding financial results. jobs.description: Employer: Polaris Inc. Expires: 10/30/2026 Marketing Internship - Summer 2027 Company Overview Polaris Inc. is a global leader in powersports and known to millions of people around the world as we offer a diverse portfolio of products and services including boats, off-road vehicles, commercial vehicles, and more. Polaris pioneers’ product breakthroughs and enriching experiences and services, that have invited people to discover the joy of being outdoors since our founding in 1954. At Polaris, we have fun doing what we love by driving change and innovation. We empower employees to take on challenging assignments and roles with an elevated level of responsibility in our agile working environment. Our people make us who we are and help create incredible products and experiences that empower us to Think Outside. Internship Program Overview The Polaris Marketing Internship (MIP) is a tailored 12-week paid summer internship designed for emerging sophomores, juniors, and seniors who are interested in pursuing a career in a leading global powersports industry. As a Marketing Intern, you will be given impactful project-based assignments that directly align with business objectives. These projects could include exposure, within our marketing division, across various segments including targeted development in these areas: Brand and Product Marketing (Brand/Lifestyle Marketing, Insights and Analytics) How you create and capture through brand and product marketing Creative and Content (Social Media, Paid Media, Partnerships, Events) How Creative and Content Creation drives business today and tomorrow Process and Go-to-Market (Ecommerce, Digital Production) How Process, Planning and communication improve work Dealer and Channel (Channel, Retail, Owner Experience, In-Market and Key Market Impact) How Dealership and Sales Channels impact our business We encourage you to embrace the adventure and be open to any placement opportunity. Being mobile and flexible will allow you to gain diverse experiences and make the most of your internship. Internship Locations Could Include: Any Polaris location across the United States. This program serves as a primary feeder into our rotational leadership development program, providing you as an intern with the foundational skills and experiences needed to excel in your career. Upon completion of the internship program, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a passion to learn may be offered a returning internship or a full-time position, depending on eligibility. As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. In addition to meaningful project work, you will participate in intentional programming and professional development offerings such as: Mentorship: you are paired with one of our DP associates for mentor support throughout your 12-weeks. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Intern Innovation Challenge: internal case study designed to promote cross functional development where you and your team will present creative and practical solutions to a real ‘Polaris’ problem to our executive leadership. Early Talent Summit Week: you participate in our 3-day event in our Wyoming, MN office. This immersive experience brings together all US interns and DPs for professional development, structured networking, a DP graduation event, inspiring executive speakers, and a thrilling team ride on some of your favorite Polaris vehicles. Community Engagement: opportunity to get involved in your local community. Final Presentations: present to our senior level leaders to showcase your career aspirations and recap your internship experience. The Selection Process: Applications are open from August -November each year. Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will typically be contacted for an initial phone screen by the end of November. Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to participate in a virtual panel interview with an identified HR business partner and functional leader. Successful candidates would move forward to an offer. You will partner with the Early Talent team in January to complete a survey that provides a deeper look at your specific interests, strengths & career goals. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. Intern Relocation Assistance: Polaris offers a relocation program for interns who qualify through our mobility vendor. jobs.description: Employer: Polaris Inc. Expires: 10/30/2026 Sales Internship - Summer 2027 Company Overview Polaris Inc. is a global leader in powersports and known to millions of people around the world as we offer a diverse portfolio of products and services including boats, off-road vehicles, commercial vehicles, and more. Polaris pioneers’ product breakthroughs and enriching experiences and services, that have invited people to discover the joy of being outdoors since our founding in 1954. At Polaris, we have fun doing what we love by driving change and innovation. We empower employees to take on challenging assignments and roles with an elevated level of responsibility in our agile working environment. Our people make us who we are and help create incredible products and experiences that empower us to Think Outside. Internship Program Overview The Polaris Sales Internship (SIP) is a tailored 12-week paid summer internship designed for emerging sophomores, juniors, and seniors who are interested in pursuing a career in a leading global powersports industry. As a Sales Intern, you will be given impactful project-based assignments that directly align with business objectives. These projects could include exposure, within our sales division, across various segments including targeted development in these areas: Dealer Enablement: Dealer Trainings & Development, Owner Connections, Fixed Operations, Low Funnel Marketing. Business Development & Channel: Dealer Policies, Dealer Distribution Footprint, Key Market Performance Management, Showroom Display & Merchandising. Product Line Sales: Program Development & Execution, Demand/Supply Analytics, Competitive Analysis, Retail Critical Thinking Leadership. Field Sales: Dealership Experience, Retail Root Cause & Countermeasure, Dealer Operations Improvement, Solicitation Ownership, Sales Enablement. We encourage you to embrace the adventure and be open to any placement opportunity. Being mobile and flexible will allow you to gain diverse experiences and make the most of your internship. Internship Locations Could Include: Plymouth, MN or Medina, MN. This program serves as a primary feeder into our rotational leadership development program, providing you as an intern with the foundational skills and experiences needed to excel in your career. Upon completion of the internship program, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a passion to learn may be offered a returning internship or a full-time position, depending on eligibility. As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. In addition to meaningful project work, you will participate in intentional programming and professional development offerings such as: Mentorship: you are paired with one of our DP associates for mentor support throughout your 12-weeks. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Intern Innovation Challenge: internal case study designed to promote cross functional development where you and your team will present creative and practical solutions to a real ‘Polaris’ problem to our executive leadership. Early Talent Summit Week: you participate in our 3-day event in our Wyoming, MN office. This immersive experience brings together all US interns and DPs for professional development, structured networking, a DP graduation event, inspiring executive speakers, and a thrilling team ride on some of your favorite Polaris vehicles. Community Engagement: opportunity to get involved in your local community. Final Presentations: present to our senior level leaders to showcase your career aspirations and recap your internship experience. The Selection Process: Applications are open from August -November each year. Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will typically be contacted for an initial phone screen by the end of November. Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to participate in a virtual panel interview with an identified HR business partner and functional leader. Successful candidates would move forward to an offer. You will partner with the Early Talent team in January to complete a survey that provides a deeper look at your specific interests, strengths & career goals. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. Intern Relocation Assistance: Polaris offers a relocation program for interns who qualify through our mobility vendor. To qualify for these services your home address must be 35 miles or more from the office where you will be working. Benefits include a lump sum (grossed up to offset tax liability), access to a relocation counselor to explain the resources available to you and aid in securing short-term housing available to you. Your responsibilities will include daily transportation to/from the office. Required Qualifications: Pursuing a bachelor’s/master’s degree in business with an emphasis in Sales, Marketing, or other related degree with an intended graduation date between August 2027-May 2029. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0 Must be able to commit to a full 12-week internship, working 40 hours per week, within one of the following date ranges: May 17th – August 6th, 2027. June 1st – August 20th, 2027. Willing and able to relocate. Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, asylee, or refugee) and not require sponsorship for employment now or in the future. Must have reliable transportation for daily commuting to and from the office. Previous experience with Microsoft Office software tools (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and Word). Preferred Qualifications: Previous Internship/Co-op experience or involvement in relevant projects. Demonstrated strengths in analysis, creative problem-solving, communication, interpersonal relationships, self-motivation, and leadership. Strong interest in long-term career development and participation in leadership development programs. Previous leadership experience in work, organizations, or classroom. Completion of at least two years of university coursework This is more than an internship - It's the beginning of your career with Polaris. We hope you're ready for the ultimate adventure!

jobs.description: Employer: Apex Park and Recreation District Expires: 10/30/2026 Job Title: Intern – Golf InstructionDepartment: Golf Operations – Indian Tree Golf ClubSupervisor’s Title: Director of Golf and Clubhouse Operations/ Golf Instruction ProfessionalDate Prepared: 9/2026 Job Status: Part-Time, Non-Exempt POSITION PURPOSE: Supports golf instruction, player development, and related golf programming at Indian Tree Golf Club. Works alongside professional golf staff to gain hands-on experience assisting with junior and adult instruction, clinics, camps, individual lessons, player-development programs, and on-course instruction. Provides support for the administrative and operational responsibilities associated with delivering quality golf programming at a public golf facility. This internship is designed to provide meaningful professional development for an individual interested in pursuing a career in golf instruction, PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, or the golf industry. ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:Assists golf professionals with individual and group golf instruction for participants of varying ages and skill levels. Supports junior golf camps and clinics, adult programs, beginner programs, and other player-development initiatives. Assists with instruction in putting, chipping, pitching, bunker play, full swing, course management, rules, etiquette, and pace of play. Prepares instructional areas, equipment, training aids, range balls, and other materials prior to programs and lessons. Assists with participant check-in, group organization, instructional stations, and program transitions. Provides basic instructional feedback to participants under the direction of professional golf staff. Assists with on-course instruction on the Par-3 and regulation golf courses. Helps create a positive, encouraging, safe, and welcoming learning environment for golfers of different ages, abilities, skill levels, and backgrounds. Assists with adaptive golf and other programs designed to make golf accessible to a broad range of participants. Assists staff in developing golf clinics, camps, leagues, lesson plans, instructional activities, and other player-development opportunities. Helps evaluate existing programs and identifies opportunities to improve the participant experience. Supports player-development efforts for juniors, beginners, women, seniors, and other developing golfers. Assists with utilizing the driving range, practice facilities, and Par-3 course as player-development resources. Assists with program registration, participation tracking, attendance, participant feedback, and program evaluation. Supports marketing and communication efforts related to golf programs and instructional opportunities. Maintains clean, organized, safe, and professional instructional and practice areas. Consistently represents the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work when interacting with participants, guests, and coworkers. OTHER DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:Gains exposure to golf shop operations, outside operations, tee-sheet management, pace of play, tournament operations, customer service, and daily golf course operations. Learns policies and procedures related to golf instruction, course access, range operations, safety, and guest service. Gains an understanding of golf program pricing, budgeting, revenue generation, expense management, and other business aspects of operating a public golf facility. Assists with golf shop and outside operations as assigned to gain a broader understanding of golf facility operations. Works with professional golf staff to establish internship learning goals and participates in ongoing coaching and feedback. May be given increasing responsibility for planning and delivering portions of clinics or instructional programs under the supervision of professional golf staff. Develops practical experience in golf instruction and coaching techniques, junior and adult programming, player development, customer service and hospitality, program management and evaluation, and public-sector golf operations. Performs other duties as assigned. SUPERVISORY DUTIES: This position does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. May assist with organizing and directing participants during camps, clinics, lessons, and other instructional activities under the supervision of professional golf staff. JOB QUALIFICATIONS -KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, etiquette, and pace of play. Interest in golf instruction, player development, golf operations, and the golf industry. Ability to effectively communicate with children, adults, guests, and coworkers. Strong customer service and interpersonal skills. Ability to create a positive and welcoming experience for program participants. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Ability to follow direction and work within the scope of assigned responsibilities and training. Ability and willingness to learn, accept coaching and feedback, and demonstrate initiative.Ability to maintain a professional appearance and demeanor. Ability to prioritize participant, guest, and employee safety. Ability to organize equipment and instructional materials and assist with multiple activities and participant groups. Ability to work a flexible schedule that may include mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays. Ability to consistently demonstrate the principles of the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Interest in golf instruction, PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, coaching, or a related field. Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, and etiquette. Experience or demonstrated ability working effectively with children and adults. CPR/AED/First Aid certification or ability to obtain certification as required.Preferred Qualifications: Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, kinesiology, business, or related program. Previous experience working at a golf course, driving range, golf camp, recreation program, or instructional setting. Previous experience working with children or youth programs. Interest in pursuing PGA membership or a career in golf instruction, player development, or golf operations.WORK ENVIRONMENT: Work is performed in both indoor and outdoor environments at Indian Tree Golf Club, including the golf shop, driving range, practice facilities, Par-3 course, and regulation golf courses. Work may be performed in varying weather and environmental conditions. The position requires regular interaction with children, adults, program participants, guests, and other employees in an active public recreation environment.PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES: Position requires the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, including walking on uneven outdoor terrain and golf course surfaces. Requires frequent bending, reaching, and movement associated with demonstrating golf skills, setting up instructional areas, and assisting with programs. Must be able to handle, move, and set up golf equipment, training aids, range balls, and other instructional materials and equipment. TRAVEL: Limited travel may be required for meetings, training, programs, or other District-related activities. NOTE: This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the job. May perform other duties as assigned.
